item.title: CVE-2026-56291 Balbooa Forms RCE Exploited; Anthropic Extends Claude Fable 5 Access
ICS Calendar Invite Phishing Hides Base64 Lures and QR Credential Harvesting
CVE-2026-56291 Exploitation, RedHook Wireless ADB Abuse, and ICS Phishing Lures
item.content:encoded:
Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-56291) Balbooa Forms Remote Code Execution via Unauthenticated File Upload — Must Read

CVE-2026-56291 is a critical, actively exploited unauthenticated file upload flaw in Balbooa Forms for Joomla that can let attackers upload and run PHP files for full remote code execution. Sites using Balbooa Forms 2.4.0 or earlier should update to 2.4.1 immediately and check for compromise.

  • CVE-2026-56291 is an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability in Balbooa Forms, the com_baforms component for Joomla, and is classified as CWE-434.
  • The vulnerability affects Balbooa Forms up to and including version 2.4.0 and can allow an anonymous attacker to upload a PHP file into a web-served directory and execute it for remote code execution.
  • The flaw has a CVSS v3.1 base score of 9.8 and a CVSS v4.0 base score of 10.0, is listed in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and is being actively exploited in the wild.
  • Balbooa fixed the vulnerability in Balbooa Forms 2.4.1, released on 9 July 2026, but sites that ran affected versions while exposed should also be checked for signs of compromise.
  • Recommended actions include inventorying internet-facing Joomla sites, identifying Balbooa Forms installations, blocking script execution in upload directories, monitoring relevant POST requests, auditing Super User accounts, and scanning upload directories for unexpected PHP files.

RedHook Android malware now uses Wireless ADB for shell access — Should Read

RedHook Android malware now abuses Wireless ADB by tricking users into granting Accessibility permissions, giving attackers shell-level access without rooting the device. This lets it silently run privileged commands, steal data, control the screen, install or remove apps, and maintain persistence.

  • A new version of the RedHook Android malware abuses Android Wireless Debugging to gain shell-level privileges without requiring a computer connection.
  • RedHook tricks victims into granting Accessibility permissions, then uses those permissions to enable Developer Options, activate Wireless Debugging, retrieve the pairing code, and connect to the phone’s ADB service through 127.0.0.1.
  • Once paired, RedHook gains shell UID 2000 privileges, which are more powerful than normal Android app permissions but are not root-level privileges.
  • The malware uses a Shizuku-based framework to execute shell commands, grant itself additional permissions, modify protected Android settings, and silently install or remove applications.
  • Group-IB reported that the latest RedHook version supports 53 server-issued commands, including screen streaming, screenshots, simulated gestures, app installation and removal, data collection, overlay creation, camera activation, and device rebooting.

The Phishing Kit That Rode In on a Calendar Invite — Should Read

A phishing email hid its entire credential-harvesting lure inside an .ics calendar invite, using embedded images, a personalized link, and a QR code to bypass body-focused email scanning. The key lesson is that defenses must inspect and render calendar attachments, including OCR and QR decoding, instead of treating them as harmless scheduling data.

  • A freight and logistics company received a phishing email whose body was nearly empty, with the malicious content hidden inside an .ics calendar invite attachment.
  • The .ics file contained a multi-page internal compliance lure rendered as embedded base64 images, along with a personalized credential-harvest link and a QR code encoding the same URL.
  • The phishing URL used the recipient’s own corporate email address in the path, allowing the landing page to appear personalized to that mailbox.
  • The message reached the inbox even though a Barracuda gateway scored it benign and Microsoft assigned it a trusted spam confidence level of -1.
  • IRONSCALES Themis flagged the message at 90% phishing confidence after rendering and OCRing the embedded images, decoding the QR code, and correlating sender and relay mismatches.

Claude Fable 5 stays free for paid users until July 19 as Anthropic buys more time — Optional

Anthropic has extended Claude Fable 5 promotional access for paid subscribers through July 19, 2026, including the 50% Claude Code weekly usage limit increase. Paid users can keep using Fable 5 within up to 50% of their weekly plan limits, but API, Free, and some Enterprise users are excluded.

  • Anthropic extended promotional access to Claude Fable 5 for paid subscribers through July 19, 2026 at 11:59:59 PM PT.
  • The promotion lets eligible users use Fable 5 for up to 50% of their weekly subscription limits at no extra cost, drawing from the same weekly usage pool as other Claude models.
  • The extension applies to Claude Pro, Max, Team, and premium seats on seat-based Enterprise plans where enabled by the organization.
  • The promotion does not apply to Free users, standard seats on seat-based Enterprise plans, usage-based Enterprise plans, or API usage.
  • After reaching the 50% weekly Fable 5 allowance, users can continue with separately billed usage credits or switch to another Claude model within remaining plan limits.
